title: Biggest Triple-Digit Run
statement:
You get a string digits made of the characters 0–9. Look at every piece of exactly three consecutive characters where all three are the same digit, like "444" or "000".

Return the largest such piece as a string. If there is none, return "". Leading zeros are allowed, so "000" is a valid answer.

examples.why: "000" is the only run of three. It still counts, even though its value is zero.
Pairs of 9s and 8s, but never three in a row.

hints: Slide a window of width three across the string.
A window qualifies when its three characters are equal. Compare it with the best so far.
Since every candidate has the same length, comparing the repeated digit is enough. Keep the largest digit seen; build the answer from it at the end.

explain.intuition:
The candidates are every window of three consecutive characters, so there are only n − 2 of them. A window counts when d[i] = d[i+1] = d[i+2]. All candidates have the same length, so the biggest one is simply the one with the biggest digit.

Keep the best digit as a number starting at −1, meaning "none found yet". That sentinel matters: using "" or 0 to mean "none" makes it easy to lose a valid "000".
steps: For each i from 0 to n − 3: if the three characters starting at i are equal, set best = max(best, digit).
Return "" if best is still −1, otherwise the digit repeated three times.
pitfalls: Treating a found "000" as "nothing found" because its value is 0 or because 0 is falsy.
Stopping the loop one window early (i < n − 3) and missing a run at the very end.
Converting candidates to numbers and returning a number, which loses the leading zeros.

solutions.title: Check each window
solutions.idea: Slide a width-three window, keep the largest digit whose window is uniform.

solutions.title: Search from 9 down
solutions.idea: Try "999", "888", … "000" and return the first that appears as a substring.

followups: Return the largest run of exactly k equal digits, for any k.
Return the longest run of one repeated digit, breaking ties by the larger digit.
